Evelyn / Sean,

I ran a quick pass on the workbook and sketched a SKU-tiering matrix (attached). Summary recommendation:

1) Baseline: L4 instances (dense inference-optimized instances) as primary compute for low-latency retrieval generation and standard-size responses (~8k context). Rationale: lower per-token cost, excellent throughput for short sequences, supports int8/4 quantized workloads.
- Typical batch sizing: 3264 depending on QPS and latency SLO.

2) Memory-heavy pool: A100 80GB or H100 80GB for sustained medium-long contexts (16k+). If your 32k-context requests are frequent, prefer H100s due to faster attention kernels for very long sequences and larger effective memory headroom for KV caches.

3) Burst / overflow: small H100 burst pool (24 GPUs) attached to an autoscale policy. Use H100 for: a) large-context generation, b) model variants that are FP16/AMP and need the extra memory/bandwidth. H100 gives best latency for 32k contexts, but its expensive if held as baseline.

4) Fallback policy: when H100s saturated, degrade to an L4-quantized variant with shorter context (trim tokens) or offload to A100s if available. This keeps service up while preventing cost blowouts.

Quantization + caching note: aggressively apply KV prefix caching for retrievals; quantize the L4 baseline where feasible. For the large model, consider QAT or 4-bit quantization only if quality is validated on your eval prompts.

Sizing heuristics (based on workbook):
- Baseline L4 cluster sized for sustained 300 qps -> estimate ~1216 L4 GPUs (depending on instance SKU/Ops).
- H100 pool for bursts/long-context: reserve 6 H100s, with autoscale to 12 for scheduled peaks (Doc: sku-tiering-matrix.csv attached).

Cost tradeoffs: in our short calc, shifting 50% of token volume to L4 reduces monthly inference spend by ~38% vs H100 baseline. But L4 tradeoff: shorter max context and some quality delta on long-context summarization.

I attached sku-tiering-matrix.csv with options: "L4-heavy", "balanced", "H100-forward". I recommend "balanced" for your pattern: L4 baseline + 6 reserved H100 (burst to 12). This gives good cost control while preserving long-context quality.

If you want, we can model concrete monthly $ at 3 commit levels (monthly, 12-month reserved, 36-month). Lauren, can you draft the pricing delta for these three commit profiles?

- Marcus
